title: Multi-model gating and early-accept evaluator for latency-aware speculative decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight runtime gating layer and an early-accept evaluator that enables latency-aware speculative decoding across multiple candidate models. This ticket covers the runtime integration, acceptance metric definitions, kernel-fingerprint-aware routing hints, and a safe fallback strategy when optimistic accepts are low-confidence. The outcome should reduce p95 token latency for common gen workloads while keeping regression on output quality under a predefined threshold.
proposal: Introduce a two-part runtime: (1) a Gating Layer that computes a fast, inexpensive score per request indicating whether to attempt cheap speculative decoding on a low-cost model variant; (2) an Early-Accept Evaluator that inspects early decode logits/entropy and decides whether the cheap path’s output can be accepted or a fallback full decode is required. The gating layer will use runtime features (sequence length estimate, recent cache hit-rate, kernel fingerprint and device thermal state) to pick candidate models and quantization levels. The evaluator uses a calibrated acceptance metric (delta-logit-confidence + n-token-consistency heuristic) with tunable thresholds. If acceptance fails, the runtime will either continue decoding on the original high-capacity model or transparently reissue a full decode depending on the policy. All decisions are logged and exposed to Console for per-route rollout control.
design_notes:
- Gating inputs: request token length estimate, user-profile affinity, recent latency tail for route, kernel fingerprint match score, KV cache hit probability.
- Candidate model pool: primary (high quality), speculative (lower-cost 4-bit/8-bit), and micro (aggressive quant).
- Acceptance metric: combine normalized delta-logit (top-1 vs runner-up over first N tokens), token-entropy trend, and repetition/coverage heuristics into a single acceptance score in [0,1].
- Thresholding: route-level acceptance threshold, with an adaptive fallback that increases conservatism when false-accept rate > X.
- Kernel hints: Gating will tag requests with preferred kernel selectors (e.g., flash-attn-v2 if sequence < 1024) to minimize runtime kernel switching.
- Config flags: enable_gating, evaluator_mode (static|adaptive), probe_sampling_rate, acceptance_threshold_override.
- Data retention: acceptance decisions retained for 30 days for offline evaluation and model calibration.
telemetry: Capture per-request fields: gated_candidate, gating_score, evaluator_score, accepted_bool, fallback_reason (timeout/low-score/kernel-mismatch), full_decode_latency_ms, speculative_decode_latency_ms, tokens_saved, quality_diff_metric (BLEU/ROUGE/logprob-delta where available). Aggregate reports: acceptance_rate, false_accept_rate (measured via sampled re-decodes), p50/p95/p99 latency with and without gating, model/kernel utilization. Expose dashboards and synthetic-eval hooks for prompt sets used in Optimize tooling.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind route-level control (console). 2) Start with sampling-only mode (log decisions but always run full decode) for 3 days. 3) Enable accept-rollback with 1% live traffic (canary) and monitor false_accept_rate and tail latency. 4) Gradually increase to 10% and 50% with automatic rollback triggers: false_accept_rate > 0.5% OR p95 increase on full-decode path > 5%. 5) Full rollout when acceptance_rate > 70% and false_accept_rate < threshold for 48h. 6) Provide emergency kill-switch in console to disable per-route gating immediately.
tests: Unit tests for gating decision logic and kernel hint encoding.
Integration test that simulates speculative accept + fallback within runtime worker and validates KV cache behavior across reissue.
Load test on staging cluster: 200k reqs/hr with mixed seq lengths to measure p95 reduction and model utilization.
Quality regression harness: sampled accepted outputs are re-decoded on primary offline to measure semantic regressions and false-accept rate.
Chaos tests: force kernel selector mismatch and model OOM to verify fallback stability.
E2E telemetry validation: ensure all fields are emitted and pipeline can reconstruct per-request trace.

acceptance_criteria: Gating reduces measured p95 token-level latency by >= 10% on target routes in canary at 10% traffic.
False-accept rate (sampled re-decode) < 0.5% on canary routes for 72h.
No increase in overall full-decode error rate or observed hallucination metric beyond baseline.
All telemetry fields documented and surfaced in Console; sampled re-decode job runs nightly and reports calibration metrics.
Fallback transitions occur within SLA (fallback added latency < 25ms median) and do not cause OOMs or worker crashes.
risks: False accepts that materially degrade user-facing quality; mitigated via aggressive sampling and re-decode checks.
Excessive kernel switching causing throughput regressions — mitigate by kernel hinting and batching alignment.
Complexity in decoding worker increases OOM risk; plan to limit speculative memory budget and run under feature flag.
Operational blind spots if telemetry events are dropped; mitigate with end-to-end validation and retained logs.
Potential security implications of telemetry content — ensure no PII flows into acceptance traces.
decisions: Use combined delta-logit + entropy trend as primary acceptance signal rather than only token-entropy.
Gating layer will be heuristic + ML-score agnostic initially to simplify rollout; future work may add learned gating models.
Speculative decodes allowed only when KV cache match probability > 30% to avoid wasted work.
Adaptive mode will back off acceptance threshold when false_accept_rate exceeds configured limit.
No persistent user-visible state will be mutated until a speculative accept is validated by the evaluator (i.e., speculative-only outputs are ephemeral until accepted).
